item.problem: Lesson 4 says the old rope has a lower elastic limit, but Lesson 6 gives the old rope a higher elastic limit extension (2.1 m vs 1.5 m for the new rope). The force at the limit is lower (441 N vs 1275 N), so this is only consistent in terms of force, not extension.

item.quote_b: Old rope: elastic limit at an extension of 2.1 m, so the largest force it can take elastically is F = kx = 210 × 2.1 = 441 N.

items.recommendation: Reword Lesson 4 to refer to the lower elastic-limit force. This matches Lesson 6 (441 N against a 784 N load), where the old rope's limit extension is greater but its limit force is lower.

Also Lesson 1 says sisal twine showed slight permanent deformation within 200 g, which conflicts with Lesson 2's claim that sisal twine returns to original length until about 300 g.
